sections.h2: What should a Sebastian homeowner know before selling fast?
sections.html:
A Sebastian owner choosing between a realtor, a private sale and a cash buyer should weigh the closing date and the repair list first. The city lies on the Indian River Lagoon in Indian River County, and the Census Bureau counts 85.2 percent of its homes as owner-occupied.

Most of the work is paperwork. The clerk records deeds, the tax collector bills each parcel, and the building department keeps permit files, so knowing who holds what saves days.

  • Request the permit history from the city's building department.
  • Learn whether a homestead exemption sits on the parcel.
  • Keep the deed, any survey and recent repair invoices together in one folder.

sections.h2: How did Sebastian grow from a lagoon settlement?
sections.html:
Sebastian began as a fishing and railroad settlement on the lagoon, and by the 2000 census it was the largest city in its county. A centennial tribute printed in the Congressional Record says the town incorporated in December 1924, became a city in 1925, and shares that year with the creation of Indian River County.

Early on the place was called New Haven after a retired minister who started the post office. Rail service came in the early 1890s, a freeze in 1894 pushed residents into commercial fishing, and Pelican Island became the first federal migratory bird refuge in 1903. In 1957 a Miami developer bought 1,345 acres to start Sebastian Highlands, and much of the city is platted from that purchase.

The same tribute lists health care, retail and food service as the leading employers.

sections.h2: What do the latest Census numbers show for Sebastian?
sections.html:
For July 1, 2025 the Census Bureau estimates 27,352 people, compared with 25,054 counted in 2020. The land area is 15.78 square miles, and 36.8 percent of residents are past 65.

sections.h2: Which Sebastian permits and repairs can slow a sale?
sections.html:
Open or expired permits are the most common permit problem, and the city building department at 1225 Main St. is where you check. Sebastian takes applications through the MGO portal and by email, and its building department phone line is 772-589-5537.

Owner-builder permits can go through the portal, but the first application has to be made in person, a requirement the city ties to Florida law. Inspections are scheduled through the portal at least one day ahead, and some air conditioning, electrical panel and plumbing inspections can be done by video.

  • Ask the building department whether any permit on your address is still open.
  • If a roof, air conditioner or water heater was replaced, find the permit and final inspection.
  • If work was done without a permit, tell the buyer or buyer's agent up front rather than at the inspection.

Cash buyers will usually take a house with unpermitted work, but they price it in. Closing out permits first can raise what a conventional buyer is willing to pay.

Sebastian's permit page says email submissions are capped at 30MB per upload, and that the city offers free remote video inspections for some inspection types. Video inspections are accepted for air conditioning replacement, electrical panel change-outs and plumbing water heater or re-pipe work, which helps when nobody lives in the house to let the inspector in.

sections.h2: How does Indian River County taxation change at a Sebastian closing?
sections.html:
Indian River County's property appraiser sets value as of each January 1, with bills going out in November. After a transfer, a capped assessment resets to just value, so a long-time owner's low bill rarely follows the house.

The homestead exemption removes up to $50,000 of taxable value, though only the first $25,000 counts for school taxes. It requires an application by March 1 and permanent residence by January 1, and renting the house out ends it.

August brings the notice of proposed taxes. Florida's printed early-payment discount is 4 percent in November, falling a point each month to 1 percent in February. At a late-year closing, your title agent divides the bill by days of ownership. Call the county property appraiser to learn what your parcel carries.

sections.h2: What do recording fees and stamp tax look like on a Sebastian deed?
sections.html:
On a Sebastian deed, Florida taxes 70 cents per $100 of price at recording, and the Department of Revenue makes each signer liable. Your contract decides who actually pays.

Under statute 28.24 the clerk adds $5 for page one and $4 for every added page, plus trust fund and technology fees.

  • Stamp tax scales with price and assumed debt.
  • Recording cost follows page count.
  • Payoffs for mortgages, liens and unpaid taxes come from proceeds.
  • Title charges differ by company.

Get the buyer's cost split itemized in writing.

sections.h2: Who tends to choose a cash sale in Sebastian?
sections.html:
Cash suits owners who value speed or condition over top price. With the Census Bureau counting 85.2 percent owner-occupancy and so many residents over 65, typical sellers include heirs, owners moving into assisted living and people who would rather not replace an aging roof or air handler.

Compare net proceeds, not headline numbers. A listing can bring more but adds showings, post-inspection repair requests and a longer wait. A cash buyer may pay less and still close sooner. Ask each one for the closing date, the party paying title and recording costs, and whether the offer survives their own inspection. Have each answer in writing before signing.

sections.h2: What should I do first if the Sebastian house is inherited or vacant?
sections.html:
Begin by confirming who has authority to sign. A house passing through an estate may need court paperwork before anyone can convey it, and the Indian River County clerk can say what has been filed. Keep utilities on and the yard tidy meanwhile.

Then ask the building department about permits, call the tax collector for any balance, and collect keys and association papers. With those in hand you can compare a listing with a cash buyer using real numbers.

sections.h2: Which Sebastian records should a buyer's agent expect from me?
sections.html:
Plan a short packet: the recorded deed, a recent tax bill, your permit list, and any association or utility account details. Add dated photos of past repairs and invoices for the roof, air conditioning and water heater.

  • Deed and any legal description or survey you have.
  • Permit numbers with final inspection dates.
  • Property tax bill and exemption status.
  • Repair invoices and warranty papers.

A seller with this packet can respond to a serious offer in a day, and cash buyers will usually return a price faster when the file is organized.

faqs.q: Does Sebastian have its own building department?
faqs.a: Yes. The City of Sebastian Building Department is at 1225 Main St. and accepts permits through the MGO portal or by email, with phone help at 772-589-5537. An owner-builder's first application must be made in person.

faqs.q: Will a buyer inherit my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. The exemption follows the qualifying owner. After a sale the buyer files by March 1 for the following tax year, and the property is assessed at just value.

faqs.q: Who pays doc stamps on a Sebastian deed?
faqs.a: Both parties are liable under the statute, and your sale contract assigns the cost. At 70 cents per $100 of price, it is collected by the clerk at the moment of recording.

faqs.q: Is a Sebastian sale still possible when permits are open?
faqs.a: Yes, with disclosure. Ask the building department which permits are open and how a buyer's title company would treat them. Cash buyers often accept open permits at a lower price.

faqs.q: What home value does the Census show for Sebastian?
faqs.a: The survey median for owner-occupied homes is $317,000 (2020-2024). It reflects owner estimates, so compare recent nearby sales before pricing.
